Good morning. The 110th plenary meeting of the General Assembly is called to order. The Assembly will begin its consideration of agenda item 63 entitled, "The situation in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine." I will now make a statement as the President of the General Assembly. Excellencies, distinguished delegates, Four and a half years have passed since the full scale invasion of Ukraine by the Russian Federation and 12 years since the illegal annexation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol. In those years, we have seen the human cost of these continuing violations of the UN Charter, even though it hardly makes headlines anymore. Yet the human toll continues to rise. During the first half of 2026, civilian casualties were 114% higher than during the same period in 2024. But these are only numbers. When we repeatedly hear casualty figures from Ukraine, as from so many other wars around the world, we can become numb to their meaning. But behind every number is a human life. with a face and a name like us. Faces and names like 20-year-old Oleksandra, who, according to Ocher, was killed in June while repairing a roof damaged in an earlier attack. His mother, Halyna, survived and returned to the rubble searching for him, repeating the last word she heard him say, "Mom." The tragedy was compounded by the fact that their family had already moved from the frontline deep in the region in search of greater safety, only for the violence to follow them. This underlines there is no safe space left. Every part of Ukraine has been a target, as we have seen with reports of the six consecutive days of strike in Kiev with nonstop day and night air raids. in a moment when school starts again. And all over the country, attacks has damaged civilian infrastructure, such as shopping centers, residential buildings, schools, and hospitals, as well as damage to inviolable properties like the honorary consulate of Latvia in the city of Sloviansk. There have also been reports of civilians being killed in the Russian Federation. Additionally, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine has documented repeated strikes affecting ambulances, rescue teams, and aid workers, including incidents in which responders were hit while returning to help. In recent weeks, reported attacks on Red Cross facilities in Ukraine have destroyed medical kits, hygiene supplies, and other relief items. The human cost alone should compel urgency. But also geographically, the war has seeped beyond Ukraine. Airspace incursions in neighboring countries are becoming more frequent. Latvia, Moldova, Romania are just the most recent ones. And the consequences of this conflict still extend far beyond Europe. For more than four years, growing threats to safe navigation in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov have carried consequences far beyond the region. These disruptions hardly make headlines anymore, but continue to have a lasting impact on food prices and access to fertilizers around the world, underlining again that this war needs to end in the interest of all of us. Therefore, the General Assembly echoes its calls for an immediate, full and unconditional ceasefire between the Russian Federation and Ukraine. the Russian Federation to immediately, completely, and unconditionally withdraw all of its military forces from the territory of Ukraine, the urgent need to end the war, the redoubling of diplomatic efforts to reduce the risk of further escalation and achieve a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace in Ukraine consistent with the UN Charter. A charter, Your Excellencies, which cannot be applied accordingly to geography, power, or political convenience. As we have seen throughout this session, not only in Ukraine, but in Gaza, Sudan, and Myanmar, wherever the UN charter or international law are violated, it is civilians that bear the cost, too often with their own lives. So today, we reaffirm previous General Assembly resolutions, not only for peace in Ukraine, but for adherence to the charter and this assembly's joint commitment to the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of every member state within its internationally recognized borders, be it in Ukraine or any other country around the world. The task before us, therefore, larger than ending the war in Ukraine. It is to defend the principles that make peace and security possible in the first place. It is about the credibility of this institution. If borders can be changed by force, if sovereignty can be set aside when inconvenient, and if the UN Charter is upheld only when politics allow, then no Member States can sleep peacefully anymore. The UN Charter protects all of us, but only when all of us are prepared to protect the Charter. I thank you. Before proceeding further, as agreed at the General Committee meeting of May 18, 2026, and announced in my letter dated May 20, 2026, I propose that the time limits for statements in the debate of this item be five minutes for individual delegations speaking in their national capacity and seven minutes for statements made on behalf of a group of States. Is there any objection to this proposal? I see an objection. In light of the objection made, no speaking time limit will be applied to the debate of this item. However, in order to be able to hear all Member States, may I kindly invite all delegations to consider their statements to hold it as brief as possible. As that, I give the floor to the first speaker in this debate, Her Excellency Marianna Betza, Deputy Minister for Foreign Affairs of Ukraine.

Civilians killed in their beds, at their home. Among those killed was a citizen of India, and this is a stark reminder that Russia's war and its indiscriminate attacks have consequences far beyond Ukraine. Representatives of indigenous peoples, religious communities, journalists, civic activists, and ordinary citizens remain subject to pressure and persecution because of their self-identification as Ukrainians. A tragic and profound example of the persecution is the story of Svitlana Loy, a 70-year-old resident of the temporarily occupied city of Tokmak, Zaporizhzhia region. She was a parishioner of the Ukrainian Greek Catholic Church and a member of the local church choir. When the Russian invasion seized the church building and handed it over to the Russian Orthodox Church, the FSB subjected the parishioners to checks. On the electronic device of this lady, the occupiers discovered records of donations to Ukrainian foundations. That was enough to invaders to charge her with so-called high treason and sentence her to 15 years. At her age, this may amount to life in prison. Ukraine calls upon all member states, international organizations, and parliamentary institutions not to recognize these illegal and sham electoral processes. These results are any mandates purportedly derived from voting conducted on the temporary occupied territory of Ukraine. We further call on states and international organizations not to send observers or representatives of this illegal electoral process is not to participate in any activities that could be interpreted as a recognition or legitimization of such voting. What we are witnessing today in the temporarily occupied territories are not just episodes of isolated violations. This is a deliberate attack to erase Ukrainian identity. Approximately 1.6 million Ukrainian children reside on the temporarily occupied territory. More than 20,000 Ukrainian children have been abducted or deported by Russia in grave breach of international law to the territory of Russia. Today, we managed to return only 2,495 young Ukrainians, and thankful to all the countries and mediators in supporting us in this. Accountability for these crimes has already reached the highest level of the Russian leadership. And I would like to recall the arrest warrants issued by ICC for Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova. The mission of experts under the OIC Moscow Mechanism has recently documented the system more broadly. the indoctrination and militarization of Ukrainian children, the imposition of Ukrainian-Russian curriculum and pro-war narratives, and the suppression of Ukrainian language and identity. Madam President, Russia's occupation policies extend far beyond political repression and violation of human rights. They are accompanied by the systematic exploitation of Ukrainian resources and attacks against the sectors that are essential for global food security. Our farmers continue to produce food and contribute to the global security. Over the past years, Russia has damaged more than 1,050 port infrastructure facilities and attacked more than 240 civilian vessels. Distinguished colleagues, the situation at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant remains extremely dangerous. This is the weapon that Russia exploits against everyone. But Ukrainians prove every single day that we are not afraid of Russia. We have successfully kicked out Russia from many regions in Ukraine. We have deoccupied more than 700 square kilometers. We're holding the contact line. Ukrainians are fighting. We should not be afraid of Russia. Russia is much weaker than it seems. And the best defense is, of course, our preparedness, our joint efforts in terms of unity, in terms of more actions and sanctions on Russia, and in terms of more military support to Ukraine. Thank you for your attention. Slava Ukraini.

Thank you, Madam President. I have the honour to speak on behalf of the Benelux countries, Belgium, Luxembourg, and my own country, the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Despite countless calls by this Assembly on Russia to end its aggression and withdraw from Ukrainian territories, and extensive UN documentation underpinning the illegality of Russian actions in occupying parts of Ukraine, The situation for millions of Ukrainians under Russian occupation continues to worsen. Arbitrary detentions and forced disappearances, torture, and the forced deportation and transfer of civilians, including children. Parents threatened with losing their children if they refused the Russian curriculum. Residents face intimidation, house searches, denial of medical care and social benefits, or detention for perceived pro-Ukrainian views for as little as a song or a flag on their phone. This is no longer about territory, but it is about people. about people who have a right to live in peace and choose their own destiny. Madam President, the Benelux countries urge Russia once more to withdraw from the Ukrainian areas it occupies, to cease attempts to erase Ukrainian identity and to grant independent monitors full access. I thank the distinguished representative of the Kingdom of the Netherlands on behalf of the Benelux countries. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the European Union on behalf of the EU and its member states, followed by Finland and Canada.

Thank you, Madam President. I have the honour to speak on behalf of the European Union's member states. The candidate countries, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Albania, Ukraine, the Republic of Moldova, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Georgia, as well as Liechtenstein, Andorra, and Monaco, align themselves with this statement. In full violation of its multilateral commitments and its bilateral agreements with Ukraine, Russia illegally annexed Crimea and the city of Sevastopol in 2014, and then proceeded to illegally occupy other Ukrainian territories both before and since its full-scale invasion in 2022. Russia's illegal war of aggression blatantly breaches the core principles and rules of the UN Charter, let us please not forget this, including the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine. It constitutes a manifest violation of international law, including the resolutions of the General Assembly. Now, for that reason alone, it must be called out by UN member states, as has already been the case on multiple occasions. Now, dear colleagues, let's focus on human rights. Despite being denied access, the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights and the UN's independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine, among others, have documented Russian actions against Ukrainians in the temporarily occupied territories. They have documented that for 12 years since 2014, Russia has been persistently committing systematic, large-scale violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms. Politically motivated persecution, arbitrary detention and arrest, extrajudicial executions, widespread and systematic torture and abuse against civilian detainees and prisoners of war, cruel, inhuman and degrading ill treatment and punishment, sexual and gender-based violence, unlawful deportations and forcible transfers of civilians, including children, and forced disappearances, violations of the right to a fair trial, suppression of freedom of expression and freedom of religion and belief, persecution of independent media, journalists, human rights defenders, and representatives of religious communities, restrictions on religious freedom, culture, education, identity, and cultural heritage, discrimination and other violations directed against Ukrainian citizens by Russia, banning of representative institutions of the Crimean Tatar people, forced passportization, unlawful conscription and mobilization of residents from temporarily occupied parts of the territory of Ukraine. Colleagues, this is the UN's documented record. Chilling. Russia imposes its own occupying administration on the temporarily occupied territory of Ukraine in violation of international humanitarian law and expropriates public and private property. You heard again the Russian representative almost proudly admitting to all this. Russia also restricts access to education in Ukraine's native language. It forces assimilation, militarization and indoctrination of minors and youth through education. Russia's aim is clear. It seems to change the demographic composition of the territories it occupies, including through the forcible transfer and deportation of civilian populations, including children. This is illegal. It is shameless and it is shameful. We call on Russia and its accomplice Belarus to immediately end the grave violation of child deportation and forcible transfer, which according to the Commission of Inquiry constitute war crimes, to stop the illegal adoptions of Ukrainian children and to ensure the immediate safe and unconditional return of all unlawfully deported and forcibly transferred Ukrainian children as per the resolution adopted by this Assembly last December. We urge the international community to join the calls for an immediate safe and unconditional release of all political prisoners and arbitrarily detained civilians by the Russian Federation, and for enhanced international monitoring of the human rights security and humanitarian situation in the temporarily occupied territories. We must ensure immediate and unhindered access by OHCHR and relevant UN special procedures, including visits to all places of deprivation of liberty, and by supporting the preservation and professional handling of evidence in line with international standards. Colleagues, Crimea, Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia, they are Ukraine. The EU will never recognize as lawful any purported annexation of Ukraine territory by Russia, nor will we recognize the forced Russification of their people and their communities, or the results of any illegal so-called elections organized by the Russian occupation administration in the temporarily occupied territory of Ukraine. The Ukrainian people, like all people, deserve a secure, independent future, free from war and free from coercion. To achieve that, the EU will continue to provide political, financial, economic, military and diplomatic support to Ukraine as it exercises its inherent right of self-defense while addressing humanitarian and needs and supporting all diplomatic efforts to bring this war to an end. Colleagues, for this to happen, Russia must stop its illegal war of aggression and its occupation of Ukraine. It must accept an unconditional, immediate, and comprehensive ceasefire. And it must come to the negotiating table to achieve a just and lasting peace in line with international law, including the UN Charter. Instead, Russia has intensified its murderous attacks against civilians in the past days, weeks and months. This is illegal. It is shameful. And it is shameless. Member states in this room must tell Russia so. Thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative of the European Union on behalf of the EU and its member states. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Finland on behalf of the Nordic and Baltic countries.

Madam President, distinguished colleagues, I have the honour to speak on behalf of the Nordic-Baltic states, Denmark, Estonia, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway, Sweden, and my own country, Finland. On August 24th, we commemorated 35 years of Ukrainian independence. That independence was endorsed overwhelmingly by Ukrainian people in 1991. It was also recognized by the international community, including Russian Federation, who thereby acknowledged Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. We condemn in the strongest terms Russia's continued war of aggression and its deliberate attacks against civilian and civilian infrastructure. According to international law, Ukraine's right to territorial integrity remains unequivocal. Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, and Crimea remain part of Ukraine. Yet most of these territories are now under unlawful occupation by Russian Federation. Madam President, Russian attacks on civilians and civilian objects have been increasing dramatically in 2026. Attacks on humanitarian workers, facilities and objects. and civilian infrastructure have also intensified, and the number of civilian casualties is the highest since March 2022. The situation of civilians in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine is particularly alarming, as they are exposed to continuous and systematic repression. The people in the temporarily Russian occupied territories of Ukraine are in an extremely vulnerable position. Crave international human rights law and international human law, humanitarian law violations against Ukrainians have been reported in growing numbers, particularly since Russia launched its full scale invasion. United Nations independent investigators have continued to report mass arbitrary detentions and widespread torture of both civilians, detainees and prisoners of war. International reports and media have further drawn attention to systematic sexual violence against Ukrainians held in Russian detention, as well as abuses against women and children in the occupied territories. Human rights organizations have documented large-scale forced transfer and unlawful deportation of Ukrainian children, and Ukrainian authorities have reported methodical efforts to eradicate Ukrainian national identity in occupied areas, including through militarization, indoctrination, and illegal adoption of children. In addition to these alarming findings, an estimated one million people in the occupied territories of Ukraine need humanitarian assistance, while humanitarian access continues to be severely restricted by Russia. We call on Russia to provide unimpeded access to the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine for the United Nations, international monitors, and humanitarian organizations. The Nordic and Baltic states reaffirm our commitment to ensuring accountability for international crimes and other violations of international law committed in the context of Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine. We remain firmly committed to the establishment of the special tribunal for the crime of aggression against Ukraine and continue our steadfast support for the efforts of the International Criminal Court. Madam President, the reality on the ground in the occupied Ukrainian territories is in stark contrast with the obligations placed on states under international humanitarian law. The occupying power is obliged to ensure the humane treatment and the basic needs of the local population and to ensure that humanitarian assistance reaches civilians whose essential needs are not otherwise met. It is clear that Russia is not striving to fulfill these obligations. We, the Nordic and Baltic states, call on Russia to immediately and fully comply with its obligations under international law. And finally, Madam President, we demand an immediate, complete and unconditional withdrawal of all Russian military forces from the territory of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. Respect for Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity is a precondition for a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in Ukraine. Respect for internationally recognized borders is a cornerstone of international law and an indispensable condition for peace and security. Our support for Ukraine's independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognised borders remains unwavering. I thank you.

I thank the distinguished representative of Finland on behalf of the Nordic and Baltic countries. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Canada on behalf of Canada, Australia and New Zealand, followed by Switzerland and Italy.

Madam President, I have the honour to speak on behalf of Australia, New Zealand, and my own country, Canada. Last week, on August 24th, we marked the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's independence. We celebrated Ukraine as it is recognized under international law, within its internationally recognized borders. Every temporarily occupied territory of Ukraine by the Russian Federation is Ukraine. We reaffirm our unwavering support for Ukraine's sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity. Russia's unprovoked and unjustifiable war of aggression violates the UN Charter. It strikes at the principles of sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence that underpin this organization. We therefore firmly reject and will never recognize the illegal so-called elections organized by Russia in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine, nor any attempt to use them to legitimize Russia's unlawful occupation. The planned September 2026 elections in these territories are the latest attempt to entrench and legitimize Russia's illegal occupation. We call on all member states to reject attempts to redraw borders by force. Colleagues, Ukrainians feel the consequences of Russia's brutal aggression every day. Ukrainians have shown extraordinary courage, but they should not be expected to endure the unendurable without consistent, principled support. In the temporarily occupied territories, human rights violations, repression, gender-based violence, and forced re-education have become a grim reality of daily life. Russia does not want the world to see what is happening in these territories. Or how it uses coercion, forced assimilation and indoctrination to erase Ukrainian identity, to entrench its occupation. Earlier this year, the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry concluded that the deportation and forcible transfer of Ukrainian children and their enforced disappearance amount to crimes against humanity. The commission has also documented what appears to be a systematic torture and ill treatment of Ukrainian civilians and prisoners of war, exposing a system of abuse and impunity. The international community must intensify all efforts to support the return of deported Ukrainian children, prisoners of war, and unlawfully detained civilians. On September 28 to 29, my own country, Canada, together with Ukraine and Norway, will convene in Toronto under the theme Pathways to Peace, the second ministerial conference on returning Ukrainian children, detained civilians and prisoners of war. The conference reflects our determination to return those unlawfully taken, support survivors and their families, and ensure that human suffering never becomes normalized. There can be no impunity for crimes committed in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine. We recognize the increasing risks posed by drone strikes and other weapons on humanitarian workers who seek to help those harmed by Russia's aggression. We condemn all attacks on humanitarian workers wherever they take place, and we call on all states to support and implement the Declaration for the Protection of Humanitarian Personnel. Russia must allow and facilitate safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access to civilians in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine in accordance with international humanitarian law. We call on countries that continue to support Russia's war effort to cease enabling its aggression and violations of international law. Russia's war extends far beyond Ukraine. Its consequences are felt in global food security, energy security, and the integrity of the international rules-based order. We welcome efforts to advance a diplomatic path towards peace and support all credible initiatives aimed at achieving a just and lasting peace. Any peace settlement must be grounded in international law, including the UN Charter, uphold Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and ensure that Russia's war of aggression can never be repeated. We stand unwavering in our commitment to help Ukraine protect its freedom, restore its territorial integrity, and rebuild a stronger future. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Canada. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Switzerland.

Mr. President, Switzerland reaffirms its support for the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognised borders. In this context, Switzerland condemns the referendum held in Crimea on March 16, 2014, as well as Russia's annexation of the peninsula and the other Ukrainian territories in 2022. These acts constitute serious violations of international law and the principles enshrined in the United Nations Charter. Switzerland remains deeply concerned about the serious and persistent violations of international humanitarian law and human rights documented by the UN in the Ukrainian territories temporarily occupied by Russia, including arbitrary detentions, enforced disappearances, acts of torture, sexual violence and the forced transfer of civilians, including children. The imposition of Russian citizenship, forced conscription and the militarisation of education constitute serious violations that must cease immediately. We also call on Russia to immediately allow safe and unimpeded access for international and regional monitoring mechanisms. in accordance with resolution 80/223 to ensure direct and credible monitoring. More generally, Switzerland is deeply alarmed by the escalation of hostilities and the growing number of reports of civilian casualties and damage to civilian property. We are particularly concerned about the intensification of air strikes and the long-range attacks targeting urban and densely populated areas in Ukraine, which are leading to an unacceptable rise in civilian casualties. In this context, we reiterate the obligation of all parties to strictly respect international humanitarian law and human rights. The principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution must be respected under all circumstances. The protection of civilians and civilian objects must remain an absolute priority and they must never be targeted. Finally, Switzerland emphasizes the need to ensure safe, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access to all populations affected by the conflict, so that aid can reach all those in need without delay. Mr. President, since 2014, the General Assembly has repeatedly reaffirmed its commitment to the Charter of the United Nations, international law and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine. Switzerland underscores the importance of fully implementing these resolutions. We once again call for the withdrawal of Russian troops from Ukrainian territory and an immediate ceasefire. Switzerland will continue to support efforts towards a just and lasting peace based on the United Nations Charter and international law. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Switzerland. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Italy.

Thank you, Mr. President. Italy fully aligns with the statement delivered by the European Union and wishes to add some remarks on its national capacity. After four and a half years of war, still no place is safe in Ukraine and in its temporarily occupied territories. And we commend the extraordinary resilience of the Ukrainian population. Since the beginning of this brutal war of aggression, Italy has strongly condemned Russia's unacceptable violation in Donetsk and Luhansk. They are violations of the principles of international law and human rights enshrined in the UN charter. Italy also reaffirms its non-recognition of the illegal annexation of the Crimean peninsula and reiterates its unwavering support to Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. Mr. President, the Ukrainian civilian population continues to bear the heaviest burden. Too many Ukrainian children remain under Russian control in temporarily occupied territories, or have been forcibly deported. Every child has the right to be safe with their families in their homeland at all times. The indoctrination and the pressure on young people into military service are Moscow's attempts to deprive the Ukrainian people of their identity and future. Immediate and unhindered humanitarian assistance must be ensured. Italy has mobilized more than 3.2 billion euros in support of Ukraine, providing assistance across the areas of humanitarian aid, reconstruction, energy, and development. We will continue to support Ukraine and stand firm alongside the Ukrainian people. In coordination with its European partners and allies, Italy will remain committed to promoting a negotiating process towards a just and lasting peace, in line with the resolution adopted last 24th February by the General Assembly. Ceasefire and a just and lasting peace remain our main priorities. The United Nations has a unique role to play, and we support all the efforts to end this war. that had disastrous humanitarian and economic consequences at the global level. I thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Italy. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the United Kingdom.

Thank you, Mr. President. It is 1,651 days since Russia began her illegal full-scale invasion of Ukraine and 12 years since her illegal annexation of Crimea. Russia's attacks are escalating, launching at least 429 missiles into Ukraine in July alone. more than double the month before. And Ukrainian civilians are paying the price. Almost 17,000 Ukrainian civilians, including 820 children, have been killed in Ukraine since February 2022. And over 51,000 civilians, including 3,000 children, have been injured. Before Russia's 2022 invasion, Ukraine accounted for 12% of global corn exports, 10% of wheat, 50% of sunflower oil. But Russian strikes on Ukraine's ports and civilian shipping have also escalated, blocking vital food supplies, contributing to higher food prices worldwide, and killing seafarers from UN member states from Africa to Asia. Mr. President, Ukraine, Russia's war in Ukraine is a clear violation of our United Nations charter and of Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. These are key principles, principles that bind every United Nations member state. Russia has invaded Crimea, and areas in Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhia oblasts and uses violence to consolidate control within them. Families are separated, children forcibly deported and indoctrinated and their names changed, Ukrainians forced to take Russian passports, Ukrainian civic leaders arbitrarily detained and disappeared, torture, ill treatment, communities left for days without water, without access to humanitarian aid, and Ukraine's cultural heritage erased and her language suppressed. Russia's occupation and attempted illegal annexations are inflicting a terrible toll on Ukrainians living in these territories. But these actions do not change Ukraine's sovereignty. nor do they rewrite her borders. And so today we call on all states to uphold the UN Charter, to reject Russia's illegal claims, to press Russia to allow humanitarian access, and to support accountability to help get Ukraine's children back home and her civilians released. The United Kingdom will stand with Ukraine as she exercises her lawful right to self-defense in accordance with Article 51 of our United Nations Charter today and for as long as it takes. We support Ukraine's call for a full, immediate, and unconditional ceasefire and a just and lasting peace. And we urge Russia to commit to the same. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the United Kingdom. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Romania.

President, Romania aligns with the EU statement. We take the floor to once more reject the war of aggression against Ukraine, a blatant violation of international law. and to speak in defense of UN Charter's core principles of independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity applicable to all nations. Through the adoption last February of the resolution support for lasting peace in Ukraine, the General Assembly called for diplomacy and peace, reconfirming the international community's commitment to those principles of the Charter. Yet again, as we speak, The aggression continues to inflict grievance and destruction upon Ukraine as Russia fails to stand up to its responsibility to stop the war, cease its occupation, and return to the respect of the UN Charter and international law. Be it in Europe or elsewhere, by now, we all felt the impact of this war. In our region alone, The aggressors intensified strikes on Ukraine's ports and commercial shipping on the Danube and in the Black Sea reignite the risk of critical disruptions to global food supply chains and maritime insecurity. Several neighbors of Ukraine, including my country, continue to face unacceptable drone incursions for which the aggressor bears full responsibility. But let us be clear, our support for Ukraine remains unwavering. Romania will stand with Ukraine and its people in their legitimate self-defense and in the exercise of their sovereign right to freely choose their future. Romania will remain a responsible and committed partner for the international community in addressing the regional and global risks of this war of aggression. And as we do so in helping Ukrainians who transited or sought shelter in our country and by facilitating the transit of Ukrainian grain to global markets. President, we reiterate our support for Ukraine's independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. Romania recalls its non-recognition of the illegal annexation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol and of the regions of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhia, and Kherson. which is flagrant violation of international law, including the UN Charter and the Helsinki Final Act. They remain an inalienable part of the national territory of Ukraine in accordance with international law. Reports about the situation in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine remain disturbing as they continue to document persistent large scale violations of human rights and fundamental freedoms, including restrictions on freedom of expression and opinion, unlawful and arbitrary detention of civilians, widespread torture and ill treatment of Ukrainian prisoners of war and civilian detainees. forced conscriptions, a systematic imposition of the occupiers educational system, and the militarization of education. The Secretary General's report on the situation of human rights in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine, including the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol, shows that civilians in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine continue to be subjected to widespread and systematic human rights violations by the occupying authorities. The Secretary General's report on conflict-related sexual violence listed the aggressor, for the first time, for committing conflict sexual-related violence against Ukrainian prisoners of war and civilians. Credible evidence has been documented, including through the Secretary General's report on children and armed conflict, on the forcible transfer and deportation of Ukrainian children in violation of the universal and inalienable right of every child to live in safety with their family, including during armed conflict and occupation. However, no statistics can fully encapsulate the grievance endured by Ukrainian civilians facing aggression and occupation. Russia must cease all such practices that violate international law and its international humanitarian and human rights obligations and to ensure unfettered access to OHCHR and other international human rights monitoring mechanisms. All unlawfully deported and forcibly transferred Ukrainian children must be returned, and we continue to support further progress through the International Coalition for the Return of Ukrainian Children and the implementation of the General Assembly resolution Return of Ukrainian Children. We support Ukraine in ensuring justice through accountability mechanisms, such as the Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine. President, This assembly expects Russia to change course towards peace and to respond to repeated calls for a full, immediate, and unconditional ceasefire and to meaningfully engage in negotiations for a just and lasting peace, matching Ukraine's proven commitment in this regard. Romania will continue to support all efforts aimed at achieving a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace in line with UN Charter and international law, with robust and workable security guarantees for Ukraine. The aggression must stop. The occupation must stop. Respect for UN Charter must be restored. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Romania. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Czechia.

Thank you, Mr. President. For more than 12 years, Russia has sought to impose its authority on territories that are not its own, occupying land, installing administrations, attempting to redraw borders. Yet one thing remains unchanged. These territories remain part of Ukraine. The Czech Republic remains steadfast in its support for the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of Ukraine within its internationally recognized borders. As the occupying power, Russia bears full responsibility under international humanitarian law for the situation in the territories under its temporary occupation. The findings of international monitoring mechanisms are deeply troubling. The Czech Republic condemns systemic violations of human rights in the occupied territories, including arbitrary detention, torture, enforced disappearances, forced assimilation, and imposed citizenship. Particularly alarming is the fate of Ukrainian children. The Czech Republic strongly condemns their forcible deportation and transfer from occupied territories and reiterates its call for the immediate return. The latest UN Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine report finds that these acts constitute crimes against humanity and grave violations of international law amounting to war crimes. Equally important is the Commission's conclusion that these crimes follow a consistent pattern. Responsibility, therefore, reaches beyond individual perpetrators. The Czech Republic therefore welcomes international initiatives to ensure accountability for the Russian crime of aggression against Ukraine. Mr. President, in the coming days, Russia will again hold so-called parliamentary elections in occupied Ukrainian territories. These will neither change the status of those territories, nor alter Ukraine's sovereignty, nor create legitimacy where none exists. They are another violation of international law, including the UN Charter, and Ukraine's sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity. These principles matter not only for Ukraine, but for every member state. If military force becomes an accepted path to territorial acquisition, the protection of the charter is weakened for all. For that reason, Mr. President, the Czech Republic will continue to stand with Ukraine for as long as necessary and to work towards a just, comprehensive, and lasting peace based on the principles of the Charter. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Czechia. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the United States.

Thank you, Mr. Chair, and I thank Ukraine for organizing this debate. The Russia-Ukraine war rages on, 12 years after Russia invaded Crimea and over four years since its full-scale invasion in 2022. In the years since, both Ukraine and Russia have paid a heavy toll. Lives lost, families separated, livelihoods and infrastructure destroyed. Only diplomacy can stem the death and destruction. Russia and Ukraine must return to the negotiating table as it is clear that no military solution exists for this war. The United States once again calls for an immediate ceasefire and good faith negotiations to return peace and stability to both countries. We support ongoing dialogue to end strikes against civilian vessels and infrastructure in the Black Sea, noting ongoing and worsening costs to global food security and oil supplies. The United States continues to play whatever constructive part it can to facilitate talks between Moscow and Kiev. Thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the United States. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Japan.

Mr. President, at the outset, Japan would like to express its heartfelt condolences for the continuing loss of many civilian lives and the damages caused by the recent Russian indiscriminate attacks across Ukraine, including in the capital, Kiev. Japan would also like to pay tribute to the Ukrainian people who are striving every day to bring peace to their homeland. Mr. President, it is deeply concerning that there is still no clear path to ending the fighting, even though four and a half years have passed since the Russian launched its unprovoked war of aggression against the sovereign state of Ukraine. Russia's aggression against Ukraine constitutes a clear and blatant violation of international law, including the UN Charter, and is an outrageous act that shakes the very foundations of international order based on the rule of law. The preservation of sovereignty and territorial integrity is of the utmost importance and any unilateral attempts to change the status quo by force must not be tolerated anywhere in the world. Also, any action that directly or indirectly supports Russia's aggression is itself a violation of international law, and all states complicit in such aggression must be held accountable. Japan is deeply concerned by the continued engagement of North Korea, including deployment of soldiers in the combat against Ukraine, which constitutes a clear violation of international law, including the UN Charter and the Security Council resolutions. Such unlawful military cooperation between Russia and DPRK is undermining peace and security in Europe, the Indo-Pacific, and beyond. Mr. President, Japan also expresses its respect for the efforts of all countries involved toward peace. Japan reiterates that Ukraine should continue to be supported in a manner that fully respects the Ukrainian people's will regarding their country's future. In order to achieve a swift and comprehensive ceasefire and a just and lasting peace, it is essential that relevant countries work together in unity and solidarity to support Ukraine, with the involvement of the United States in calling on Russia to take positive actions immediately. Mr. President, Japan will never waver in its consistent position of standing by the people of Ukraine. Japan has been steadily providing assistance to Ukraine and will continue to promote support for Ukraine and the sanctions against Russia in coordination with the international community. Japan will also continue to work on public-private partnership assistance for recovery and reconstruction in Ukraine.

With a view to strengthening Ukraine's social and economic resilience.

I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of Japan. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of the Republic of Korea.

Thank you, Mr. Chair. Pandemic years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, The war continues to exact a devastating human toll with no end yet in sight. As civilian suffering deepens, the urgency of protecting lives and bringing this war to a close has only grown. Against this backdrop, I would like to highlight three points. First, civilians must not continue to bear the cost of this war. We are alarmed by a sharp rise in civilian casualties, with the United Nations reporting that in July alone, at least 437 civilians were killed and more than 2,600 injured, the highest monthly civilian death toll since May 2022. Recent large-scale Russian missiles and drone attacks continue to damage civilian infrastructure. Civilians must be protected and all parties must comply with international humanitarian law. Particular attention must also be paid to the temporarily occupied territory where civilians remain especially vulnerable to violations of their fundamental rights and threat to their safety. We hope to see the tangible progress, including the safe return of possibly transported children and other civilians separated from their families and homes. Second, the Republic of Korea remains seriously concerned about continuing military cooperation between Russia and DPRK. Despite repeated calls for its cessation, this cooperation continues unabated, including arms and ballistic missile transfers, troop deployments, and other forms of military support. Such cooperation continues to prolong the war while posing a serious threat to international peace and security. This military cooperation, including arms and ballistic missile transfers, is in clear violation of relevant Security Council resolutions and runs counter to the spirit and principles of the UN Charter. The Republic of Korea therefore urges Russia and the DPRK to immediately cease their unlawful military cooperation. Third, diplomatic engagement is essential to bring this war to an end. This is the war that should not have begun and must now end without further delay. As the war drags on, the human toll continues to mount, devastation deepens, and the international order built on the principles of the UN Charter comes under increasing strain. The Republic of Korea supports diplomatic efforts by the United States and other relevant actors to bring the war to an end. and calls on all parties to engage constructively and demonstrate the political will needed for sustainable peace. Mr. Chair, the human cost of this war have already been immense, and the damage inflicted on civilian life and infrastructure is equally profound. Continued hostility will only deepen this suffering. and make the path to peace and recovery ever more difficult. This war must, therefore, be brought to an end as soon as possible. For its part, the Republic of Korea will continue to work constructively with the international community in support of efforts to bring this war to a close. We will also remain committed to addressing humanitarian needs and supporting recovery and reconstruction. I thank you.
I thank the distinguished representative of the Republic of Korea. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of Portugal.

Thank you, Mr. President. Portugal aligns with the statement delivered by the European Union and would like to add the following in its national capacity. Portugal stands with Ukraine and the Ukrainian people providing assistance at all levels, both bilaterally and with our European Union and United Nations partner, and we will continue to do so. But our objective is not to prolong the war, it is to secure peace. We are alarmed with the increasing intensity of the Russian attacks, and we are appalled that the number of civilian deaths in July reached the highest level since May 2022, and that child casualties were highest since April 2022. The suffering should stop. We need an immediate and conditional and comprehensive ceasefire. We need space for serious negotiations. We must give diplomacy a chance. My country, therefore, supports all genuine diplomatic efforts towards a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace. firmly anchored in the Charter of the United Nations, a pathway that this General Assembly has called for and supported in several resolutions. That means respecting Ukraine's sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity within its internationally recognized borders. Territorial acquisition by force cannot be accepted or recognized. Occupation cannot become normalized and peace cannot be sustainable if it rewards aggression or legitimizes annexation. These are concrete steps that can and must be taken now. Prisoner exchanges must continue. Civilians unlawfully detained must be released. Humanitarian access must be ensured. And the thousands of Ukrainian children unlawfully deported or transferred must be returned immediately, unconditionally, and safely, in line with the resolution overwhelmingly adopted by this Assembly only a few months ago. These are tangible steps towards building the minimum confidence required for diplomacy to succeed. At the same time, the reality on the ground remains devastating. Civilian casualties continue to rise, including among children. Attacks affecting homes, hospitals, energy and water infrastructure deepen human suffering and undermine the conditions for recovery. International humanitarian law is not optional. Civilians, humanitarian personnel and civilian infrastructure should be protected. As the Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs recently reminded us, Warfare technology may evolve, our legal obligations do not. We remain equally appalled by the human rights violations documented by the United Nations in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine. Occupation does not suspend international law. The principles at stake here extend far beyond Ukraine. They are foundations of the international order on which every member state, large or small, depends. And the consequences of this war also extend far beyond Europe. Food insecurity, pressure on global markets, and threats to maritime security in the Black Sea affect countries far away, particularly the most vulnerable. Freedom and safety of navigation must therefore be protected, and food supply chains should not become again a casualty of war. Our task now is to turn those principles into results and to go from words to action. The objective must remain clear, a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace, peace that ends suffering, peace that restores rights, and peace that upholds rather than weakens the universal principles of the charter that binds us all. I thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the distinguished representative of Portugal. I now give the floor to the distinguished representative of China.

President, as we gather again, the situation in Ukraine remains unresolved.

Since GA last considered the issue of Ukraine, the situation on the ground has not only failed to ease, but has instead escalated further, with frequent violent attacks resulting in civilian casualties.

The hostilities have seriously impacted third party countries, which is a source of a deep concern and pain. China calls on the parties concerned and the international community.

To work together to promote an early ceasefire, an end to the fighting and a political resolution to the crisis.

First, China urges an end to all attacks targeting civilians.

And calls on the parties to remain calm and exercise restraint, strictly observe international humanitarian law, protect the safety of civilians and civilian infrastructure.

Avoid harming civilians and civilian assets in third countries, and work towards keeping hope alive for an early realization of.

Peace. Second, dialogue and negotiations are the only way out of this crisis. parties concerned must not abandon their efforts simply because negotiations are difficult, nor refuse to engage with each other simply because differences exist.

Instead, they should remain patient, demonstrate goodwill, strive to get the talks off the ground, gradually build mutual trust and consensus, and in the end work together to reach a comprehensive, lasting and binding peace agreement.

Third, despite.

Tremendous difficulties on the ground, Russia and Ukraine have consistently moved forward with the exchange of POWs and the remains.

Of fallen soldiers, which is indeed commendable.

Every humanitarian operation carried out helps build up mutual trust between the two sides, which in turn has the potential to push.

Dialogue and negotiations one step forward.

Fourth, Countries in the region and the international community at large should voice more rational calls for a ceasefire.

And an end to.

The war, as well as for reconciliation and negotiations, and undergo more diplomatic efforts to build trust and facilitate mediation.

What the parties should do is not only to reflect on history and address the root causes, but also look to the future, striving to properly address each other's legitimate security concerns and to promote the establishment of a balanced, effective, and sustainable regional security architecture. Sixth.

The continued spillover effect of the crisis has triggered secondary issues including shipping security, energy security, food security and the security of cross-border infrastructure.

The international community should unite to jointly safeguard the stability and smooth operation of global production and supply chains.

President, China's position on the Ukrainian issue has been consistent and clear.

President Xi Jinping has.

Solemnly pointed out that the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all countries should be respected, the purposes and principles of the UN Charter be upheld, the legitimate security concerns of all countries be taken seriously, and all efforts conducive to a peaceful resolution of.

The crisis be supported.

These four shoes constitute China's authoritative position and fundamental guiding principles on the Ukrainian issue.

China has maintained close communication with the parties and the international community, working in its own way to.

Encourage reconciliation and promote the dialogue, thereby playing its due role in building consensus among all parties and advancing a political resolution to the crisis.
